subject.title: refactor: unify the embedded-agent fallback run-entry across all four pipelines

question: After the failing type-test check is diagnosed and redacted runtime evidence demonstrates the shared helper on representative fallback and terminal paths, should this cross-pipeline refactor be accepted as the canonical lifecycle owner?
rationale: The protected maintainer signal and the choice to centralize four intentionally different runtime contracts require an owner to judge whether the abstraction boundary remains appropriate after proof is complete.

options.title: Require proof and clean validation
options.body: Keep the canonical helper direction, but require a redacted real execution artifact plus a resolved `check-test-types` result before merge.

options.title: Narrow the refactor
options.body: Retain only the common fallback mechanics and move any path-specific terminal or settlement behavior back behind narrower owners if runtime proof exposes a contract mismatch.

recommendation.title: Require proof and clean validation
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical helper direction, but require a redacted real execution artifact plus a resolved `check-test-types` result before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence ties this person to the proposed shared lifecycle boundary; broader current-main ownership needs history confirmation.
